newsitem.title: CHINA: China urges Taiwan to lift ban on air links.
newsitem.headline: China urges Taiwan to lift ban on air links.

text.p: China on Monday renewed an overture to rival Taiwan and urged the island to lift a decades-old ban on direct air and shipping links, saying the curbs increased costs by several billion U.S. dollars a year.
"Direct air and shipping links between the two sides is unstoppable," the weekly magazine Outlook said in its latest edition.
"We hope to use the Chinese government's resumption of sovereignty over Hong Kong (on July 1)...to open a new air route between the two sides," the official magazine said.

Taiwan has banned direct air and shipping links with China since the Communists defeated and drove the Nationalists into exile on the island in 1949. Trade is routed through third countries, most of it going through Hong Kong.

Taiwanese investors have poured an accumulated $60 billion into China and set up 30,000 businesses by the end of 1996. Two-way trade totalled $20 billion last year, with Taiwan enjoying a $10 billion surplus, Outlook said.
Taiwanese made about 1.6 million trips to China last year. Chinese have made 200,000 trips to the island since 1988, the magazine said.
Curbs on direct air and shipping links waste precious time, increase the costs of Taiwanese businessmen by billions of U.S. dollars a year and reduce their competitiveness, it said.

In January, Chinese and Taiwanese shippers held talks in Hong Kong and agreed to ease the ban by allowing ships to leave Taiwan ports for the southeastern Chinese cities of Fuzhou and Xiamen. Ships are still banned from sailing directly from Chinese ports to Taiwan.
Taiwanese businessmen are eager for direct air and shipping links, but Taiwan fears lifting the ban would make the island an economic hostage to China.

Tensions between China and Taiwan had eased since the late 1980s, but ties took a turn for the worse last March, when China conducted war games and missile tests close to Taiwan in the run-up to the island's historic presidential elections.
